summary: Console Suggestions beta: “High risk” label is too vague — customer requests concrete reasons in UI
description:
Issue summary:
Customer is evaluating the new Console > Optimize > Suggestions view (beta). They’re seeing multiple suggestions labeled “High risk” but the UI does not explain *why* the risk is high in concrete terms. Customer feedback is that the label reads as a blocker (“we can’t adopt something labeled high risk without a reason”) and reduces trust in the feature.

Impact:
- Customer cannot make a decision on whether to trial the suggestion.
- Risk label is perceived as opaque; adoption drops because the team can’t justify/mitigate.
- CS/SEs are forced to provide ad-hoc explanations and paste internal rationale in emails.

Where observed:
- Console (prod) > Optimize > Suggestions (beta) > Suggestion list shows risk chip “High risk”.
- Detail drawer currently has savings estimate + some basis-of-estimate, but no “risk rationale” section (or it is too generic).

Customer request:
- Add “Why this is high risk” (or similar) with 2–4 human-readable rationale bullets.
- Prefer reasons grounded in measurable signals (latency headroom, workload variance, cache hit-rate confidence) and include which signal(s) drove the classification.
- Clarify reversibility / rollback expectations (e.g., “can be reverted immediately” vs “requires rollout”).

Expected behavior:
- High/Medium/Low risk labels should have an explanation visible in the detail drawer.
- Explanation should be consistent with ADR-0274 and guardrails so Support doesn’t contradict product.

Actual behavior:
- Risk chip shows “High risk” with no actionable explanation (customer perceives this as vague/subjective).

Notes:
- This is beta feedback but also a UX gap with real adoption impact.
- Customer explicitly stated they do not want confidence and risk collapsed into one label unless rationale is shown.

Support context:
Raised after a customer call where they asked “high risk because of what — latency? quality? caching instability?” and requested a concrete list for auditability/trust. This ticket tracks the customer-facing UX improvement request and the shipped change to include rationale bullets.
comments: 2026-02-14 09:12 (Dev Patel, Support) - Opened per Northpeak feedback on Suggestions beta. They like savings estimate but said: “High risk is not actionable. We need to know what’s driving that label.” Asking for a short list of concrete reasons in the drawer.

2026-02-14 10:03 (Rachel Kim, Enterprise CS) - Confirming this came up in our weekly cohort check-in. They have strict internal change review; if we can’t provide rationale, they won’t trial any “high risk” suggestion in prod. Requested: show the top drivers + whether it’s reversible.

2026-02-14 11:21 (Tessa Morgan, Design) - Agree we should show rationale in the detail drawer. Proposed structure: Risk level chip + “Why this risk level” section with 3 bullets, then “Assumptions” below. Copy should avoid guarantees. I’ll align with ADR-0274 wording and keep it consistent with what the model can provide.

2026-02-14 12:40 (Jonas Weber, Applied ML) - From the pipeline side we already have explanation fields available (risk_level + rationale bullets + assumptions) in the risk scoring stub. If UI isn’t rendering them, that’s on Console integration. Drivers we can safely show: low latency headroom vs p95 SLO, high workload variance (seq length/TTFT variance), low confidence in cache hit-rate uplift. We should not imply quality risk unless we have quality signal present for that tenant/workload slice.

2026-02-15 09:18 (Dylan Brooks, Eng - Console & tooling) - Action: update detail drawer to render “risk_rationale” bullets when present, and show a fallback message when missing. Will coordinate with Chloe on BFF schema pass-through. Tracking in redwood#18681; design sign-off from Tessa.

2026-02-16 14:07 (Chloe Martin, Console backend) - Confirmed API has fields: risk_level, risk_rationale (array), risk_assumptions (array). BFF was only passing risk_level. Fixing BFF mapping + adding schema validation to avoid silently dropping explanation fields.

2026-02-18 16:55 (Dev Patel, Support) - Sent interim workaround to customer: excerpted the risk taxonomy (ADR-0274) and explained typical drivers (latency headroom + workload variance + confidence). Customer acknowledged but reiterated they want it in-product for audit trail / shared understanding.

2026-02-20 10:26 (Nora Ahmed, Console feature engineer) - Deployed behind suggestions_beta flag: detail drawer now includes “Why this is {risk}” with bullets and “Assumptions” section. Also improved empty state when telemetry is insufficient so we don’t show risk without basis. Related: redwood#18731 for messaging.

2026-02-21 08:41 (Rachel Kim, Enterprise CS) - Customer confirmed the new rationale bullets address the concern. They specifically called out that seeing “Low latency headroom vs p95 SLO” and “High traffic variance” made it clear what they need to evaluate internally.

2026-02-21 09:05 (Dev Patel, Support) - Closing. Follow-up request from customer: ability to export suggestion detail (including rationale) as JSON/PDF for change review. Logging separately if needed.
resolution: Implemented risk rationale disclosure in the Suggestions detail drawer. Console now renders risk rationale bullets and assumptions when provided by the suggestions service / risk pipeline, and BFF passes through explanation fields (previously only risk_level was shown). Shipped behind suggestions_beta flag; customer validated in prod. No further action required for this ticket.
internal_notes: Root cause: Console BFF schema mapping dropped risk explanation fields, leaving UI with only the risk label. Fix included (1) BFF pass-through + schema validation, (2) drawer UI section for rationale bullets, (3) safer fallback copy when rationale is missing. Ensure future schema changes follow ADR-0275/ENG-2410 versioning approach so explanation fields don’t regress.
